statement: Seven peptide regions (domains 1-7) are common to all elements
note: The central structural claim of the founding partition.

statement: The seven domains contain 178 amino acids in total
note: Xiong counted across all RT classes; this substrate is one class, so agreement in magnitude is informative and exact agreement is not expected.

statement: 42 conserved positions were identified within the seven domains
note: Same caveat as H02: a different sequence set, the same criterion.

statement: RT subdomains 0-7 are equally conserved within the mitochondrial and bacterial groups, 90 and 94 residues respectively
note: Measured on this very alignment by its own authors, so it is the closest thing to a ground truth this gate has.

statement: The catalytic YxDD motif lies in subdomain 5
note: An ordering constraint that numbers the recovered blocks without importing any modern boundary.

statement: The 4/5 spacer varies from 1 to 179 amino acids
note: Tests whether the gap between recovered blocks 4 and 5 behaves as the source says a spacer does.

statement: The 7/X spacer ranges from 0 to 235 amino acids
note: Requires domain X to be located, which this gate does not reconstruct.

statement: Most RNA viruses lack a complete domain 6
note: The classes Xiong names are absent here; what is testable is whether one recovered block is systematically less occupied than the others.

statement: LtrA RT0 is the N-terminal fragment M1-R85, and RT1/7 spans R86-R364
note: Independent and structural. Used only to test a reconstruction built without it; it may constrain or falsify, never define.

statement: Subdomain 0 is conserved only between group II intron and non-LTR RTs
published_value: group II intron and non-LTR only
note: Untestable on a group II intron only alignment: there is no non-LTR comparison class here. Reported OUT_OF_FRAME rather than scored.

statement: The subdomain labels were taken from earlier work and adjusted to the boundaries of conservation seen in this alignment
note: If the conservation boundaries in this alignment do not reproduce a seven-way partition, that bears directly on what the published labels rest on.
